item.title: Incarico di ricerca: SYSMAGRAD: Coupling Synthetic Supramolecular Materials with Controlled Chemical Gradients - Ref. 129/26/IR (Politecnico TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-10 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

Leveraging on innovative computational techniques, the SYSMAGRAD project investigates the coupling between supramolecular materials of various nature and concentration gradients. Biomaterials naturally couple with the chemical gradients that surround them, giving rise to properties such as autonomous motion, self-catalysis, and regeneration. Engineering synthetic materials, such as supramolecular polymeric systems, that can couple in an analogous way with external chemical gradients is a topical challenge, which requires a deep understanding of the coupling mechanisms between complex molecular systems and the solution environment in which they are immersed. The research activity is part of the FIS2 project DIGITCELL (“A digital twin for efficient solar cells”), which aims to build simulation-based digital twins of photovoltaic devices in which the parameters of the device model are computed from first principles instead of being fitted to measurements. In line with the research program, the research activity will focus on the development and application of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to reconstruct the background of thermospheric mass density and identify its perturbative components. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Photoluminescence, Raman, and near-field spectroscopic studies on III-V nanowires (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-19 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-03 Fisica sperimentale della materia e applicazioni

As part of the ERC StG NANOWHYR project (grant number: 101042349), we will investigate the photoluminescence and Raman signal generated by III-V nanowires (GaAsN, InN, InAsP, etc.) involved in the ERC project in a near-field mode, integrated with different substrates. We will assemble a near-field microscope and connect it to a new photoluminescence setup and both pulsed and continuous lasers. We will also investigate the possibility to use the near-field tip to locally anneal hydrogen in hydrogenated III-V nanowires, to form localized emitters.

Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

The research will investigate interface instabilities and quantum transport between two coupled Bose–Einstein condensates in relative motion and characterized by distinct order-parameter structures. Finite-temperature effects will be described through a self-consistent kinetic many-body framework that couples the dynamical evolution of the condensates to a quantum kinetic equation for the thermal components, including mean-field interactions, collisions, and particle exchange between the condensate and thermal cloud. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Development of Algorithms for Real-Time Data Analysis for Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Projects (Istituto Nazionale di Astrofisica)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-01 23:59
Institution: Istituto Nazionale di Astrofisica, Bologna
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-05 Astrofisica e cosmologia, fisica dello spazio, della terra e del clima

The research focuses on the development, implementation and validation of data analysis algorithms for ground-based and space-based gamma-ray astrophysics experiments, with particular emphasis on real-time processing. Activities include the development of software tools and methods for scientific data analysis, the application of statistical and computational techniques, the analysis and interpretation of algorithm results, and the investigation of data acquired by Cherenkov telescopes and satellite-borne gamma-ray instruments. The research will be carried out within the gamma-ray astrophysics projects of INAF-OAS Bologna, particularly in connection with CTA and AGILE activities.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Characterizing the dynamics of innovation in human activities and biological systems (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-09 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

Innovations and novelties concern, at a fundamental level, human activities, social behaviours, and biological systems. The vast majority of these systems are intrinsically open systems: new, previously unknown elements may continuously emerge. Statistical and dynamical regularities are shared by systems featuring innovation, pointing to general, i.e., non-system-specific, mechanisms underlying the innovation process. We will deepen the study of a class of Pólya-urn-based models that reproduce many of the empirical behaviours observed in real-world systems, while searching for novel relevant observables to characterise the latter.
